title: The Impact of Photo Appeal on the Willingness to Pay for Hotel Stays – Survey and Experiment
authors: Eberhard Feess; Lucrezia Rosato; Thomas Schilling
design: Two studies; same hotels and descriptions, photo-appeal contrast
extraction: The publisher describes own willingness to pay in Study 1 and incentivized estimates of others’ willingness to pay in Study 2. The abstract reports higher willingness to pay with higher-appeal sets.
limitations: Full text not obtained. Sample size, stay duration, baseline, uncertainty interval and exact incentive mechanism are not established here. The abstract’s approximately £248 contrast is not a nightly rate or realized revenue estimate.

title: An Exploration of the Effects of Photograph Content, Photograph Source, and Price on Consumers’ Online Travel Booking Intentions
authors: Yoojin Shin; Breffni M. Noone; Stephani K. A. Robson
design: Two experiments on photograph content, source and price
extraction: The abstract reports greater perceived information value for product-focused than experience-focused photos. Information value mediates the content–intention relationship; price and source also matter.
limitations: Restricted full text. Sample size and effect uncertainty not available in the abstract. Booking intention is not a purchase. This motivates examining factual identification, without establishing novelty.

title: The role of photograph aesthetics on online review sites: Effects of management- versus traveler-generated photos on tourists’ decision-making
authors: Ben Marder; Antonia Erz; Robert Angell; Kirk Plangger
design: Four controlled online experiments; accepted manuscript
extraction: Professional and amateur aesthetics are examined with review context, risk aversion and photo mixtures. The paper reports appeal and booking-intention differences whose patterns depend on context.
limitations: Accepted manuscript read through the university’s PDF. Self-reported intentions; no completed hotel transactions established. Manipulated production aesthetics do not by themselves isolate room-information clarity.
source_locator: Accepted manuscript printed pp. 2, 15–31 (university PDF adds cover page); repository publication metadata

title: The effects of the aesthetics and composition of hotels’ digital photo images on online booking decisions
authors: Pedro Cuesta-Valiño; Sergey Kazakov; Pablo Gutiérrez-Rodríguez; Orlando Lima Rua
design: Observational image classification with hotel-level booking indicator
extraction: The study collected 1,350 photos from 225 four-star Barcelona hotels; three images failed embedding. Its target was the modal last-hour booking badge observed four times, six hours apart, over one day.
limitations: Hotel-level public badge is not image-level conversion or transaction revenue. Images share hotel outcomes; confounding and clustered observations limit causal interpretation. The paper itself proposes adding room rate and guest ratings as controls.
source_locator: Methodology: Data collection; Results: Image embedding; Limitations

title: Using Eye Tracking to Obtain a Deeper Understanding of What Drives Online Hotel Choice
authors: Breffni Noone; Stephani K. A. Robson
design: Exploratory eye tracking during naturalistic online hotel search
extraction: Participants planned a hypothetical three-day weekend and stopped before booking. Images and descriptions received attention during deliberation. Sessions lasted 60 minutes; participants had booked online within six months.
limitations: Small exploratory sample; exclusions related to eye-tracking equipment. Attention is neither comprehension nor causal conversion evidence. No actual purchases occurred in the task.
source_locator: Cornell Hospitality Report, September 2014, printed pp. 9–12

title: Effects of hotel website photographs and length of textual descriptions on viewers’ emotions and behavioral intentions
authors: Diego Bufquin; Jeong-Yeol Park; Robin M. Back; Marco W. W. Nutta; Tingting Zhang
design: Website photograph number and description length; structural equation modeling
extraction: The university abstract relates photo count and description length to enjoyment, stress and booking intention. It reports that enjoyment is associated with greater booking intention.
limitations: Full text not available from the repository. The repository lists 2019 in-press metadata; the publisher issue is May 2020. No room-comprehension or realized-revenue result is established.
source_locator: University repository abstract; publisher issue metadata
